about: Each SDK runs every scenario against fake_collector.py with its HTTP sink. It sends events with sequence_number 1..events, closes the sink, then checks: every write returned within limits.write_ms; close returned within settings.shutdown_budget_ms + limits.close_margin_ms; nothing raised; the collector got at least one request, except in mode 'down'; every accepted sequence number was sent, where accepted leaves out client_report events (SPEC §11.4.7), which the collector counts apart; and accepted + the SDK's drop count >= events, since an event can be both delivered and counted but never neither. 'expect' pins exact numbers where the mode makes them certain. Where 'expect' has 'reports', the runner, not the SDK, first waits for the collector to have the expected accepted and reports, with GET /_received?accepted=A&reports=R&wait_ms=limits.report_ms, since close stops reports. The collector counts only reports that come after it accepted an event, since SPEC §11.4.7 sends one only after a delivery. Mode 'down' starts no collector: the SDK sends to port 1 on 127.0.0.1, where nothing listens.
